interactions.content: Sent standard first reminder to the accounts@ mailbox for INV-1877 (Rs 3,10,000, due 2 Apr). Attached invoice copy and ledger statement, asked for expected payment date. No auto-reply, no response.
Second reminder to accounts@ for INV-1877, now 12 days overdue. Same template with 'gentle follow-up' in the subject line. Read receipt never came back. Still no reply after five working days.

Called Ramesh Iyer (Head of AP) on his desk line around 11:30. He said he had not seen either email because accounts@ is checked by a junior who files vendor mails into a folder and only raises them when asked. He asked me to WhatsApp him the invoice and said he would put it in Friday's payment run. Pleasant, 6-minute call.
Ramesh replied to the WhatsApp with the invoice PDF within ten minutes: 'Got it. Will push through in Friday run, you should see NEFT by Saturday.'
NEFT of Rs 3,10,000 received from Meridian Retail, narration 'INV-1877 full'. Paid three days after the call, exactly as Ramesh said.
First reminder for INV-1942 (Rs 2,65,000, due 5 Jun) sent to accounts@ using the standard template. No response.
Second reminder to accounts@ with Ramesh Iyer in cc this time. Still nothing from the mailbox, and Ramesh did not reply on email either. Learned later he had over 400 unread mails that week.

Called Ramesh. He was candid: two new store openings in June had squeezed cash and the finance director had capped vendor payouts for the month. He offered to pay in two parts, Rs 1,50,000 next Friday and the balance in the first week of July. I accepted and confirmed the plan on WhatsApp afterwards.
NEFT Rs 1,50,000 received, narration 'INV-1942 part 1'. First instalment paid on the day promised.

Balance Rs 1,15,000 received for INV-1942. Ramesh sent a WhatsApp the same afternoon: 'Balance cleared, sorry for the delay this month.' Invoice fully settled 28 days late, both instalments on the agreed dates.
First reminder for INV-2041 (Rs 4,20,000, due 22 Aug) sent to accounts@ using the standard template. As with every previous invoice, no acknowledgement.

Escalated in writing. Sent a firm notice to Ramesh Iyer with accounts@ and our sales manager in cc: subject 'INV-2041 - final reminder before credit hold', stating that further dispatches would be suspended and interest at 18% p.a. would be applied per our terms if payment was not received within 5 working days. Skipped the usual call because the amount was large and month-end was approaching.

Ramesh replied within the hour, clearly angry. Quote: 'After four years of business I did not expect a threat of credit hold and interest as the first thing I hear from you on this invoice. For the record, our warehouse reports 12 cartons short on the 24 July delivery. We are putting INV-2041 on hold until the shortage is reconciled and I would ask that future communication go through a proper conversation, not a legal-sounding email.' He copied his finance director.

Called Ramesh to de-escalate. Apologised for the tone of the 2 Sep email and walked him through the delivery: the consignment went in two vehicles, and the 12 'missing' cartons were on the second lorry, received and signed for on 26 Jul on challan DC-7712. Shared the signed challan on WhatsApp during the call. He checked with the warehouse, accepted the shortage claim was a filing error, and said he would release the payment. He also mentioned, almost in passing, that 'there are some changes happening on our side and I may not be the one running the next payment cycle.'

WhatsApp to Ramesh checking whether INV-2041 made it into the Friday run, and mentioning INV-2058 was now also due. Message showed a single grey tick and never delivered. By 20 Sep the number no longer showed a WhatsApp Business profile.

Called Ramesh's desk line. Reception said Ramesh Iyer left Meridian Retail on 15 September. Accounts payable is now headed by Kavita Menon, who joined from a Bengaluru retail group. Reception gave her extension and email (kavita.menon@meridianretail.example) and said she does not use WhatsApp for vendor matters.

Introduction email to Kavita Menon: welcomed her, summarised the account (four years, two open invoices INV-2041 Rs 4,20,000 and INV-2058 Rs 1,15,000), noted the September shortage claim had been resolved with Ramesh on 8 Sep, and attached the signed challan DC-7712 and current ledger. Asked how she prefers to be contacted.

Kavita replied: 'Thank you for the summary, this is helpful. I am still getting up to speed on open vendor balances and there was no handover note on this account. I have your ledger and the challan. I prefer email so there is a record, and if you need to speak I am available Tuesdays and Thursdays after 3 pm. I cannot commit to a date yet but will revert within the week.' Polite and professional, no commitment to a payment date.
Standard first reminder for INV-1901 (Rs 1,98,000, due 1 May) to billing@. No reply.
Second reminder to billing@ with Suresh Babu in cc. Nothing back. Sales rep later said Suresh 'does not really do email'.

Sent Suresh a short WhatsApp with the invoice number and amount. He replied in 20 minutes: 'Sir payment will go on 31st only. Our retailers pay us month end, every month same story. Don't worry, 31st confirmed.' Friendly, unbothered by the reminder.
RTGS Rs 1,98,000 received on the last working day of May, as promised on WhatsApp. Suresh forwarded the UTR on WhatsApp without being asked.

Went straight to WhatsApp for INV-1988 (Rs 3,40,000, due 3 Jul), skipping email. Suresh replied: 'This month tough, monsoon returns from retailers very high. Can I do three parts? 15th, 31st, and 14th Aug.' Agreed to the plan on the spot and sent a one-line confirmation of the three dates and amounts (1.2 L, 1.2 L, 1.0 L).
Rs 1,20,000 received, first of three instalments on INV-1988, on the agreed date.

Final Rs 1,00,000 received for INV-1988. Second instalment of Rs 1,20,000 had landed on 31 Jul. All three instalments paid on the exact dates Suresh proposed. No reminders were needed between instalments.
New collections trainee sent the standard email reminder for INV-2047 (Rs 2,76,500, due 30 Aug) to billing@, unaware of the account's history. Predictably, no reply.
WhatsApp to Suresh about INV-2047. Reply in 40 minutes: '30th September confirmed, full amount. Will send UTR same day.' Promise-to-pay logged for 30 Sep.

Sent first reminder for INV-1935 (Rs 2,10,000, due 8 Jun) to ap@apexoffice with Priya Nair addressed by name. Priya replied the next morning: 'Noted, GRN is cleared and this is in the 20 June payment batch.' Payment of Rs 2,10,000 arrived on 19 Jun. Email works well with this customer when the goods receipt is clean.

Priya responded to the 18 Aug reminder for INV-2039: 'Procurement has flagged that 4 of the 12 ergonomic chairs arrived with cracked castor bases. Vikram Shetty has put the GRN on hold. I cannot release any payment on this invoice until he clears it. Please coordinate with him directly.' She attached photos from the site.

Called Vikram Shetty (Procurement). He confirmed the damage was transit-related, wants replacement chairs rather than a credit note because the client fit-out is already in use. Agreed we would dispatch 4 replacements and collect the damaged units. He was firm but reasonable, and said the rest of the order was fine.

Emailed Priya and Vikram: 4 replacement chairs dispatched on docket BLR-44812, expected delivery 14 Sep. Asked whether the undisputed portion of INV-2039 (desks, storage units and the 8 good chairs, Rs 2,32,000) could be released ahead of the replacement sign-off.
Rs 2,32,000 received against INV-2039. Priya's covering email: 'Undisputed portion released as requested. Balance Rs 1,16,000 will be processed once Vikram signs the GRN for the replacement chairs.'

Asked Priya for a status on the replacement sign-off. She replied same day: 'Replacements were received on 15 Sep but Vikram is on leave until 5 Oct and no one else can sign the GRN. Balance will go in the first batch after he is back.' Dispute effectively resolved, payment now gated on one person's return.

First reminder for INV-2055 (Rs 1,92,000, due 9 Sep) to accounts@ using the standard template. No reply, no bounce. This is the first time Orbit has been late; their May and June invoices were paid on time without contact.
Second reminder to accounts@. Still no response. We do not have a named AP contact or a phone number beyond the switchboard, so there is nothing else to try yet.
